archetype.name: Pocket Passer (reined-in gunslinger)
archetype.definition: A 38-year-old timing passer who wins from a clean pocket with quick, rhythm throws over the middle and in the red zone, but still pays for his old downfield risk-taking with interceptions.

report.headline: The 2025 fireworks are gone; this is efficient, conservative Stafford with downfield picks.
report.take:
Stafford in his 18th season is a good but not dominant quarterback. His 0.119 EPA per dropback ranks 18th of 54, far above a league average of -0.021, and he is on pace for 4,459 yards and 32 touchdowns. That is a step down from 2025, when he led the league in yards and touchdowns with 0.228 EPA per play (8th). It looks almost exactly like his 2023 (0.121) and 2024 (0.115) lines. The career record suggests last year was the outlier and this is the norm.

The main change is how often he takes chances. His aggressiveness has fallen from 19.3% to 13.44%, back into the 12-13% band he lived in from 2021 through 2024. Intended air yards sit at 7.63, short of the sticks, and the ball comes out in 2.7 seconds. That rhythm explains why he is pressured on only 15.1% of dropbacks (5th) and sacked on 3.9% (5th). The production comes from the 10-19 yard window, where he posts 0.346 EPA and 58.8% success, and from the red zone: 16 touchdowns against one interception, at 0.305 EPA. Behind him, McVay's offense runs well (5th in rush EPA) and the defense ranks 3rd in EPA, so Stafford rarely has to carry a game.

The raw lines hide two flaws. First, the interceptions: his 10 rank 51st of 54, and 8 of them came on throws of 10+ air yards. His deep ball completes 27.8% at -9.6 CPOE, so when he does push it, the misses are costly. Second, third down: -0.142 EPA and a 37.9% conversion rate with an average of 7.2 yards to go. The recent 3-0 run also flatters him. Over the last three games he has averaged 211.3 yards, 51 below his season rate, with CPOE 3.1 points worse. His EPA per dropback (0.139) held up, but the team is winning with less asked of him.

From here, two things pull against each other. Davante Adams has been the most efficient target on the roster at 0.378 EPA per target and is reportedly aiming to return for the Packers game. But the interior line just lost starting center Coleman Shelton (doubtful, expected to miss several weeks) and guard Steve Avila (out), and backup center Dylan McMahon went on IR. Expect the efficient, low-volume version to continue. Adams adds some ceiling, and a thin interior adds risk to the clean-pocket formula everything rests on.

strengths.title: Clean pocket, almost no sacks
strengths.body: He is pressured on 15.1% of dropbacks and sacked on just 3.9%, both 5th in the league, four points under the league sack rate. The cause is his quick, defined reads plus a line that ranks well in hits allowed. That is partly scheme and partly an 18-year veteran's processing. The processing lasts; the protection piece is now in question with two interior starters hurt.

strengths.title: Intermediate middle is his money zone
strengths.body: Throws of 10-19 air yards return 0.346 EPA with 58.8% success, and throws over the middle return 0.261 EPA, the best of his three directions. This is McVay's play-action and crossing-route menu thrown with anticipation, and it has been a Stafford trait for years. It is sustainable, though the intermediate window also produced 5 of his interceptions.

strengths.title: Red-zone finishing
strengths.body: He has 16 touchdowns and one interception inside the 20, at 0.305 EPA and +3.5 CPOE. The short-area accuracy (74.4% on 0-9 yard throws with 13 TDs) carries over near the goal line. The rate will cool a little, but the skill and the play-calling behind it are real.

concerns.title: Downfield throws still produce interceptions
concerns.body: Eight of his 10 interceptions came on throws of 10+ air yards, and the deep ball (36 attempts) completes 27.8% with -9.6 CPOE and 3 picks. He takes far fewer chances than last year, but the ones he takes are failing more often than they hit. With an interception rate ranked 35th and 10 picks ranked 51st, this is a real flaw, not just the cost of aggression. His career shows he has always carried some interception risk.

concerns.title: Third downs stall drives
concerns.body: On third down he is at -0.142 EPA with a 37.9% conversion rate. The 7.2-yard average distance is part of it, but his short-of-the-sticks tendency (air yards 1.15 short of the marker overall) leaves little margin in obvious passing downs. Better early-down work or Adams' return could help. Otherwise this is a structural drag.

concerns.title: Volume is shrinking as defense wins
concerns.body: Over the last three games, all wins, he averaged 211.3 yards on 31.3 attempts, 51 yards below his season rate, with CPOE 3.1 points worse. A top-three defense and a strong run game mean fewer late passing scripts. That is good for the team and a ceiling problem for his box score, and it will likely continue.

trend.note: Game-level EPA has swung from +16.4 (Giants) and +14 (Arizona last week) to below zero in four games. The aggregate is steadier than that: EPA per dropback over the last three is slightly above his season mark, while yardage and accuracy have dipped.

nextGame.headline: Adams may return, but a patched interior line meets Green Bay
nextGame.body:
Green Bay's defense ranks 7th in EPA and 7th against the pass, and it is 3rd in explosive pass rate allowed. That squeezes the big plays but leaves room for the intermediate rhythm game Stafford is living on. The Packers hold quarterbacks to the 6th-fewest fantasy points, yet they have been generous to opposing WR1s and stingy to tight ends. The ball should flow to Nacua rather than Higbee. Green Bay's run game ranks last in EPA, and Josh Jacobs is out. Against the Rams' league-best run defense, the Packers may have to throw, which could hand the Rams another controlled script and keep Stafford's volume moderate. The game is indoors after a bye, with 10 days' rest.

Availability is the story on both sides. The Rams are missing center Coleman Shelton (doubtful, expected out several weeks) and guard Steve Avila (out), both 90%+ snap starters, and backup center Dylan McMahon is on IR. That is the biggest threat to Stafford's low-pressure profile against a defense ranked 10th in sack rate. Adams is targeting this exact game for his return, which would restore his most efficient target. For Green Bay, linebacker Zaire Franklin (99% of snaps) is out, which weakens the middle of the field, where Stafford is at his best. Micah Parsons is listed out but could debut after the bye if he clears a couple more hurdles. If he plays, the edge rush and a weakened Rams interior become a real problem.

keyMatchups.title: Depleted interior line vs pass rush
keyMatchups.body: With the starting center and left guard out and the backup center on IR, the Rams will play deep reserves inside. Stafford's season rests on a clean pocket, and Green Bay's 7.1% sack rate is top-ten. Interior pressure up the middle is the hardest kind for a pocket passer to escape.

keyMatchups.title: Nacua against a soft WR1 profile
keyMatchups.body: Green Bay has let lead receivers score 2.3 PPR points over their averages (26th of 32), and its WR target share runs above the league's. Nacua has drawn 93 targets at 0.204 EPA each. With Franklin out of the middle, the crossers and digs Stafford likes should be open.

keyMatchups.title: Explosive-play wall vs his shaky deep ball
keyMatchups.body: The Packers allow few explosive passes (3rd), and Stafford's 20+ yard throws are completing at 27.8% with three interceptions. If Adams returns, his 0.378 EPA per target is the Rams' best chance to beat that. Without him, forcing it deep is how this game turns into a turnover game.

nextGame.watch: Who snaps the ball, and how often Stafford gets moved off his spot early. If the patched interior holds, the rhythm game works. If not, his third-down and interception problems get worse.

restOfSeason.body:
The efficient core should hold: quick timing, low sack rate, intermediate throws and red-zone finishing have all held up across his Rams years. This season reads like his 2023-24 form, not last year's run. What caps the box score is context. A top-three defense and a strong run game keep attempts in the low 30s when the Rams lead, as the recent stretch showed. Adams' return would lift the yardage and big-play ceiling. The interior line injuries are the main downside risk, because his whole profile depends on the pocket staying clean.

Expect something like 225-265 passing yards and 1.5-2.1 touchdowns a game. Interceptions should settle toward 0.6-1.0 a game as he keeps his aggressiveness down, though the downfield misses will not disappear. His red-zone touchdown rate is the likeliest number to cool. Fantasy output should land around 14-19 PPR points a game, with almost nothing added on the ground.
swingFactors: How long Shelton and Avila are out
Game scripts controlled by the Rams defense

confidence.note: Ten starts and an 18-year track record anchor the profile, but the line injuries and Adams' return are fresh unknowns.
